title: John close: all the books in the world (John 21:20–25)
hookLine: if everything were written down, the world couldn't contain the books
carry: the world could not contain it
last: THE WOUND IS OPENED, GENTLY, SO IT CAN HEAL.

cards: Peter has just been forgiven, given a job, and told follow me. And the very first thing he does? He turns around, sees the beloved disciple walking behind them, and asks: "Lord, and what shall this man do?"
What about him? It's a very human question: barely handed a calling of his own, Peter is already checking someone else's. Is his harder?
Easier? Does he get the better ending? Jesus's answer is short, and it's the last thing he says in John's Gospel.

teach.h: WHAT IS THAT TO THEE? FOLLOW THOU ME.
teach.b: "If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me." Your path is yours.
Then John clears up a rumor. People had started saying this disciple would never die. John says, Jesus never said that.
He only said, if I want him to stay, what is that to you? It seems the community needed that set straight, perhaps after the beloved disciple had died.

teach.h: WE KNOW HIS TESTIMONY IS TRUE.
teach.b: Then a signature, of sorts: "This is the disciple which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his testimony is true." We. Other voices, standing behind the witness, vouching for him.

And the last verse, with a wink: "there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written."

teach.h: BIBLIA: MORE BOOKS THAN THE WORLD COULD HOLD.
teach.b: A Gospel that began with the Word, before time, ends with books, more than the world could hold. The Greek word is biblia, little scrolls, the word that gave us Bible.
Sixty-five days in this Gospel: the Word and the Lamb. Come and see, under the fig tree, water into wine. Born from above, for God so loved.
A Samaritan woman at a well.

teach.h: THE WORLD ITSELF COULD NOT CONTAIN THE BOOKS.
teach.b: Bread of life, light of the world, the truth will set you free. The good shepherd, Lazarus, Jesus wept. A grain of wheat, feet washed, Tertullian, many rooms, the vine.
Then the garden, the fire, ecce homo, tetelestai. And Rabboni, shalom, my Lord and my God, Jerome, feed my sheep. Tomorrow, a letter, written by Paul, from prison, full of joy.

how: In many churches, readings from John fill the weeks of Lent and Easter, and some Christians read the Gospel straight through as a whole.

practice: Think back over these weeks in John and find the scene that actually stuck, not the one you think should have: a word, a line, a face.
Shape one sentence about it in your own words, something you've seen, wondered or felt; if you pray, it can be a line of thanks, and if you're learning, it can be a question.
